note: Adapted from the original English description in Snyder 1922, where the species is described as Anoplotermes gracilis, new species; the genus has no soldiers, and the original records only the alate (Winged adult), with no description of the worker. Male alate holotype Cat. No. 24578, U.S.N.M.; type locality Ancon, Canal Zone, Panama, 19 April 1919 (month 4), collected by H. F. Dietz on the outer wall of a wasp nest on a royal palm (Dietz Acc. No. G. 475a, Hopk. U.S. No. 14124h); further specimens taken at light in Panama City. In the original, the measurement "pronotum width 0.65" carries the parenthetical note "curled", i.e. that measurement was taken from a curled specimen.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Paler and shorter-bodied than A. ater. The postclypeus is more than twice as wide as long and projecting, whereas in A. ater it is three times as wide as long and not projecting at all; the compound eyes are less projecting than in A. ater; the mandibles are shorter than in A. fumosus (those of A. ater are rather long, but still shorter than in fumosus); the head is narrower than in A. ater, and the abdomen narrower and less robust than in ater.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, widest at the compound eyes, wider than the pronotum, rounded behind, longer than wide, densely covered with long golden-yellow hairs; fontanelle indistinct. Postclypeus yellowish brown, more than twice as wide as long, projecting, hairy. Labrum yellow, long, nearly triangular, rounded at the tip, hairy, reaching the tips of the mandibles. Compound eyes black, large, nearly round, very close to the lower margin of the head, less than one compound eye diameter from both the anterior and the posterior margin of the head. Ocelli large, long, deeply sunken (upper margin projecting), less than their short diameter from the compound eyes and placed obliquely to them. Antennae yellowish brown, slender, 15-segmented, hairy; 1st segment long, stout, cylindrical; 2nd shorter, nearly clavate; 3rd very short; 4th longer but shorter than the 2nd; terminal segment slender, nearly oval. Pronotum yellowish brown, slightly wider than long, not wider than the head, widest at the anterior margin, anterior and posterior margins straight, the sides sloping angularly backwards, the anterior region with dark brown markings, the lateral margins with long hairs. Mesonotum and metanotum dark brown, with long hairs, posterior margin concave. Wings dark, ciliate at the margins, 8.5 mm long; media usually branched apically, with 0—3 branches; cubitus (submedia) with 9—11 branches; media closer to the cubitus than to the costa. Abdominal tergites dark brown, densely covered with short and long golden-yellow hairs. Legs yellowish brown, slender, rather long. Measurements (mm): alate total length 9.5—11; dealate total length 5.5—6.5; head length (to tip of labrum) 0.90—1.0; pronotum length 0.402—0.500; hind tibia length 0.800; forewing length 10.5; wing scale length 0.500; head width (at compound eyes) 0.65—0.75; compound eye diameter 0.202—0.207; pronotum width 0.65 (curled); forewing width 2.65.
